name: Acme Corp — security review and pricing (AE)
turns: Hi Dana, hi Priya. Jordan briefed me on the discovery call, so I will not make you repeat yourselves. Priya, let us start with security.

Thanks. To be clear, Acme requires a SOC 2 Type II report from any vendor, Type I is not enough. I also need to know whether Northwind supports SSO through Okta, and where customer data is stored, because Acme's EU subsidiary needs EU data residency.
Northwind has a current SOC 2 Type II report, Okta SSO via SAML, and an EU hosting region. I will send the report and the SSO guide over right after this call.
Good. Send them to me directly and I will review within a week.

On commercials: Northwind's 25,000 dollars a year list price is a problem for Acme. As I told Jordan, anything over 20k needs Mark Chen to sign off, and I would rather not open that door for a pilot. Is there an 18k pilot tier for six seats?
I can put together an 18k pilot proposal for six procurement seats with the option to expand to the full team in Q2.
That would work. For what it is worth, Vendorly came back with a discount, but the team still remembers how clunky their workflow was.

Noted. Action items on my side: SOC 2 Type II report and Okta SSO docs to Priya by October 3, and an 18k six-seat pilot proposal to you by the same date. Dana, could you bring Mark into the next call?
I will try to get Mark on the next call. Email me the proposal, not a calendar invite.
rep_notes: Acme Corp pilot tenant must be provisioned in Northwind's EU region (EU subsidiary data residency).
Competitor Vendorly offered Acme a discount on 2026-09-30; Acme's team still considers Vendorly's workflow clunky.
